premise.claim: PR title: 'optim(utils): sanitize and clamp subpaths to handle path escaping'; commit message: 'prevent escaping mount roots'. The PR body is an unfilled template, so the claim is taken from the title/commit.
premise.reportedComponent: not stated (no linked issue; 'fixes #XXXX' placeholder left in the body)
premise.evidence: On base 05f06659 a fluid_sub_path of '../../../../../hostonly' makes NodePublishVolume publish a mount source outside the FUSE root and the pod reads 'HOST-ONLY-CONTENT'. Contained at head 70d75f12 (clamped) and at head 076f0ba9 (rejected with InvalidArgument). See results/L1_plugins_BASE.txt and results/round2_head.txt.

findings.summary: checkSymlinkFile (nodeserver.go:177) does os.Lstat(mountPath), inspecting only the FINAL component. A subPath whose EARLIER component is a symlink escapes: 'evil' is rejected, 'evil/inner' publishes a mount source resolving outside the FUSE root and the pod reads host content. The new spec added in this PR only covers the single-component case.
Bites guard for N1: the single-component symlink subPath must stay rejected. Its contrast with N1 is what shows the guard is incomplete rather than absent.

Upgrade regression, widened in round 2. A persisted non-local fluid_sub_path (reachable on base via dataset://ns/ds//sub-c) is now rejected at NodePublishVolume, at getMountInfo (runtime_helper.go:112) for the sidecar path, and at GetPhysicalDatasetSubPath (dataset.go:77) via checkDatasetMountSupport, so an existing Dataset also stops reconciling. The PV attribute is only set at creation, so upgrading never rewrites it.

mutator_default.go:337 hands the subPath to GetPostStartCommand, which interpolates it into a bash -c string (check_fuse_default.go:132). filepath.IsLocal rejects traversal but accepts shell metacharacters, so the postStart hook executes an attacker-supplied command. Verified by observing the injected side effect.

The shipped sidecar gate 'while [ ! -e  $ConditionPathIsMountPoint/*/$SubPath ]' is unquoted and contains a glob. A subPath with a space makes [ return 2, so the loop is skipped and the script exits 0, reporting a missing subPath as present. csi/shell/check_mount.sh:48 was already hardened; the two copies diverged.
Bites guard for F2: an ordinary missing subPath must still be reported missing (exit 2).

NodePublishVolume did not consult MOUNT_ROOT before 6432fdfe; checkPathUnderMountRoot now fails closed without it. The Helm chart defaults runtime.mountRoot to /runtime-mnt so a default install is fine. Informational.

Round 2 added three specs with real assertions, resolving the substance. Remaining gaps: the pre-existing 'should append subpath to fluid path' spec still discards both results, nothing covers the F3 back-compat case, and the symlink spec covers only the single-component case.

notVerifiedByTest.summary: dataset.go:56 and :61 return the identical 'should only have one mount' error, but :61 guards a different condition (the single mount is not a dataset:// reference).

The PR title still says 'sanitize and clamp' though nothing is clamped at 076f0ba9 and pkg/utils is net -36 lines. Commit 076f0ba9 is titled 'fix comment' but changes a function signature, adds validation and updates four call sites.

Tenant reachability of P0 was established by code reading, not a live cluster run: GetPhysicalDatasetSubPath is the only producer of the PV attribute, mountPoint carries only MinLength=5, and there is no validating webhook on Dataset.

liveNote: No live layer needed: the symlink publish method makes the computed mount source observable via os.Readlink, and AnnotationSkipCheckMountReadyTarget=MountPod routes past check_mount.sh. A live run would additionally confirm the end-to-end tenant path (Dataset -> PV attribute -> pod), currently asserted from code reading only (F7).

resolvedFindings.note: Validation is now consistently reject-at-every-boundary instead of silent clamping at three sites and rejection at one. This was the round-1 recommendation.
utils.CleanSubPath and its 10-case unit test were deleted at 076f0ba9, so the overclaiming doc comment is gone with it.
